lenses.lens: macOS window/tab plumbing (TabManager_mac.mm, WindowManager_mac.mm, simple_handler_mac.mm, cef_browser_shell_mac.mm NSWindow hierarchy) — role assignment, browser-id↔tab-id attribution, overlay-as-tab reachability, multi-window OnBeforeBrowse coverage.

findings.title: Gold-pill payment safeguard is silently ABSENT for auto-approved payments made from any tab in a non-primary (Cmd+N / dock-reopened) window
findings.mechanism: The gold-pill tab badge is the documented 'primary visual safeguard against silent payment abuse.' Both fire sites — createAction silent-approve (the CefPostTask in HandleIpcWalletCall) and BRC-121 firePaymentSuccessIpc() — funnel through OnWalletCallSuccess, which sends the payment_success_indicator IPC to SimpleHandler::GetHeaderBrowser() ONLY. GetHeaderBrowser() returns WindowManager::GetPrimaryWindow()->header_browser — the PRIMARY window's header, hardcoded, never derived from the paying browser's own window. On macOS each window from CreateFullWindow (reachable via Cmd+N newWindow:, newWindowFromDock:, applicationShouldHandleReopen:, and the Cmd+T no-active-window fallback) gets its OWN header browser (new SimpleHandler("header", wid)). SendTabListToWindow filters tabs by window_id, so a window's React header only knows its own tabs, and useTabManager.ts lights the pill only when tab.id === browserId within that list. Result: a dApp in a tab in window 2 that triggers an auto-approved payment (within the user's pre-authorized caps) sends the IPC to window 1's header, whose tab list lacks that tab.id, so the match fails and NO pill appears on ANY window. A hostile dApp can deliberately operate from a second window to suppress the only visual confirmation that money moved. GetTabIdForBrowserIdentifier itself is correct (Tab::id is a monotonic non-recycled global counter) so the pill is dropped, not shown on the wrong tab. Payment still completes and is recorded in Rust's activity log; only the user-facing safeguard is defeated. Cross-platform in principle but squarely inside the macOS multi-window plumbing this lens covers.
findings.experiment: On macOS (or Windows): create a wallet, approve a dApp so payments auto-approve within limits. Open a SECOND window (Cmd+N). Load the same dApp in the second window's tab and trigger an auto-approved createAction (or BRC-121 402 paid retry). Check the debug log for 'OnWalletCallSuccess fired ... tabId=N' (N = second window's tab id) and confirm NO gold pill renders on any tab strip. Negative control: repeat the identical payment from a PRIMARY-window tab and confirm the pill DOES render. The delta proves the safeguard is window-scoped to the primary header.

lenses.ruledOut: RULED OUT / verified sound: (1) Role assignment on every macOS browser-creation site — all CreateBrowser calls in cef_browser_shell_mac.mm and TabManager_mac.mm pass an explicit role string (header, settings, wallet, backup, brc100_auth, notification, cookiepanel, omnibox, downloadpanel, profilepanel, bookmarkspanel, siteinfopanel, tablistpanel, menu, and tab_{id} for tabs). No macOS browser is created with an empty/absent role (grepped: no SimpleHandler(\"\") or SimpleHandler()). (2) The trust boundary does NOT key off role anyway — the default-deny IPC gate keys off ResolveIpcOrigin(frame) (hodos::OriginFromUrl, scheme-anchored, userinfo-stripped, fail-closed to opaque-origin.invalid), so a role-confused browser is still origin-gated. The 'trusted overlay direct wallet request' bypass in GetResourceRequestHandler requires BOTH IsWalletHostPort(url) AND role in {wallet,wallet_panel,settings,backup}; a tab is tab_{id} and cannot obtain it. G1 frontend-serving keys off hodos::IsInternalFrontendUrl(url), not role. (3) Overlay-as-tab: overlays are separate NSWindows/NSViews with overlay roles; ExtractTabIdFromRole returns -1 so OnAfterCreated/OnBeforeClose never register them with TabManager. No path turns an overlay into a tab. (4) Multi-window OnBeforeBrowse coverage: every macOS content browser is a SimpleHandler; GetRequestHandler() returns this, so OnBeforeBrowse fires for all. Farbling-seed and adblock branches are gated on ExtractTabIdFromRole != -1 / frame->IsMain(), correctly scoping to tab web content and exempting trusted 127.0.0.1:5137. MoveTabToWindow destroys+recreates via CreateTab (fresh CreateBrowser -> full OnBeforeBrowse), so reparenting cannot smuggle a browser past the hook. (5) GetTabIdForBrowserIdentifier cannot misattribute across windows (globally-unique, non-recycled Tab::id). (6) window.open()/NEW_POPUP popups inherit the opener tab's SimpleHandler+role and get re-registered as the opener's tab browser in OnAfterCreated (a real attribution/UX quirk — opener's tab->browser pointer is overwritten) but the popup is still untrusted web content under the same origin IPC gate, gains no trust, and moves no money on its own; latent, not a bypass. RELATED-BUT-NOT-A-BYPASS: the payment-confirmation/domain-approval/cert-disclosure modal on macOS always parents to g_main_window (window 0) via CreateNotificationOverlay's addChildWindow, identical to Windows' g_hwnd primary parenting, so a modal for a payment originating in a secondary window renders over window 0 (or, if window 0 is closed-but-not-released while the process stays alive, over an invisible window). This FAILS CLOSED — the modal still needs an explicit click and otherwise times out and denies — so it is UX/visibility degradation, not a silent money-move.

findings.title: macOS ships with the Chromium sandbox unconditionally OFF while Windows ships it ON — a renderer compromise reads wallet.db and talks to 127.0.0.1:31301 as a native client, behind every C++ gate
findings.mechanism: `cef_browser_shell_mac.mm :: main` sets `settings.no_sandbox = true;` with NO condition, justified by a stale comment ("Disable sandbox on macOS for development (requires code signing otherwise)") — but release.yml Developer-ID-signs the app, both helpers and hodos-wallet/hodos-adblock, so the stated precondition no longer holds for the shipped build. Windows is the opposite: `cef_browser_shell.cpp :: RunHodosMain` sets `no_sandbox` ONLY `if (!sandbox_info)`, and S2 (2026-08-04) verified 14 renderers at UNTRUSTED integrity. Consequence for the money path: every macOS renderer hosting arbitrary web content runs unsandboxed with full user privileges. A Chromium RCE — the exact threat the sandbox exists for — then (a) reads `~/Library/Application Support/HodosBrowser/wallet/wallet.db` directly, i.e. the money DB and every address/UTXO/tx row, and on a legacy no-PIN wallet the plaintext `wallets.mnemonic`; (b) opens a plain TCP socket to 127.0.0.1:31301 as a native client, which bypasses the ENTIRE C++ trust boundary this phase hardened — the C2 default-deny `IpcMessageAllowedFromWebPage` gate, `hodos::OriginFromUrl`, `IsInternalOrigin`, `IsPaymentEndpoint` header stamping — because all of those gate the `wallet_call` IPC channel in the browser process, not the loopback socket; (c) forges `Origin: http://127.0.0.1:5137` and any `X-Requesting-Domain`, since actix CORS and `domain_trust_mw` can only trust headers. Windows contains the same RCE at UNTRUSTED integrity, which cannot open %APPDATA% or forge a wallet-internal origin. beta.3 SHIPS macOS, so this is a live release-gate item, not a hypothetical.

findings.title: Every macOS helper process opens the profile history SQLite DB read-write — the banner comment that says it does not, and says "on macOS this init never ran at all", is FALSE
findings.mechanism: `simple_render_process_handler.cpp` carries two long banner comments asserting the fix: "The render process deliberately does NOT open the history database" and "it never worked on macOS at all — the renderer-side init is #ifdef'd out, so history.* silently returned empty there". The removal was made inside `#ifdef _WIN32`. But the macOS renderer is a SEPARATE executable with its own entry point, `cef-native/mac/process_helper_mac.mm :: main`, and that main still calls `HistoryManager::GetInstance().Initialize(cache_path)` unconditionally, before `CefExecuteProcess`. `HistoryManager::Initialize` calls `OpenDatabase()`, which is `sqlite3_open_v2(..., SQLITE_OPEN_READWRITE | SQLITE_OPEN_CREATE)` followed by `CREATE TABLE` DDL. So on macOS EVERY helper — renderer, GPU, plugin, alerts — holds a read/write sqlite3 handle on `<AppSupport>/<HodosBrowser|HodosBrowserDev>/<profile>/HodosHistory` for its whole lifetime, and CREATES the file and schema if absent. That is precisely the capability the Windows comment says had to be removed, and it is a WRITE handle, so a compromised web-content process can also forge or erase history. Two compounding defects in the same 30 lines: (1) the path is resolved through `AppPaths::GetAppDirName()`, i.e. `getenv("HODOS_DEV")`, read in a CHILD process — the exact anti-pattern `simple_app.cpp :: OnBeforeChildProcessLaunch` forbids in writing ("⛔ A SWITCH, never an env var. A sandboxed child does not reliably inherit our environment — that exact assumption made EnforceDevSafeguard fail in every child"), so if the env is not inherited a DEV helper silently CREATEs and writes the PRODUCTION history DB — the dev/prod isolation break this lens was sent to look for; (2) `profileId` falls back to `"Default"` whenever `--profile=` is absent, so any helper launched without the switch writes into Default's history regardless of the active profile. It also means `AcquireProfileLock`, which only the browser process holds, does NOT establish single-writer discipline over the profile's SQLite files on macOS.

findings.title: macOS has no kill-on-parent-death for the money process: after a browser crash or Force Quit, hodos-wallet survives Keychain-unlocked on 31301 with no modal consumer and no gold pill — Windows guarantees teardown via a job object
findings.mechanism: `cef_browser_shell.cpp :: LaunchWalletProcess` deliberately assigns hodos-wallet.exe to a job object with `JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE`, with the comment "covers crashes, Task Manager kills, and any exit path we miss". The macOS counterpart, `cef_browser_shell_mac.mm :: SpawnWalletServer`, is a bare `posix_spawn` with no job-object equivalent (no kqueue NOTE_EXIT watch, no getppid poll in the wallet, no launchd job); teardown is only the cooperative `kill(g_wallet_server_pid, SIGTERM)` inside `ShutdownApplication` and the `stopPid` helper. So any non-cooperative exit — SIGKILL, Force Quit, a browser-process crash, a GPU-process-induced abort — orphans the money process. The orphan is materially worse than an idle daemon: `main.rs` auto-unlocks via `crypto/dpapi.rs :: dpapi_decrypt` (macOS Keychain, service HodosBrowser, account wallet-mnemonic), so it holds the decrypted mnemonic in `WalletDatabase.cached_mnemonic` and serves the full wallet API on 127.0.0.1:31301 indefinitely. With no browser, a Rust 202 PENDING has NO modal consumer (`HttpRequestInterceptor.cpp :: OpenPromptModal` is gone) and the gold-pill emitter `OnWalletCallSuccess` is gone — so the only decisions that can complete are `PermissionDecision::Silent` ones, i.e. auto-approvals inside the caps, and they complete with zero user-visible signal. Worse, the next launch does not start clean: `SpawnWalletServer` begins with `QuickHealthCheck()` (GET /health, matches "ok") and ADOPTS whatever is listening, so a wallet the user thinks they quit is silently re-attached. Same call shape also means any local process that binds 31301 first becomes the browser's wallet.

findings.title: SpawnWalletServer's dev fallback walks out of the .app bundle and can resolve the money binary to a user-writable path under $HOME
findings.mechanism: `cef_browser_shell_mac.mm :: SpawnWalletServer` resolves the wallet as `exeDir + "/hodos-wallet"`, and on `access(..., X_OK) != 0` falls back to `exeDir + "/../../../../../../rust-wallet/target/release/hodos-wallet"` and then a five-`..` variant, posix_spawn'ing whichever is executable. These are relative walks with no containment check that the result is still inside the bundle. For `/Applications/HodosBrowser.app/Contents/MacOS` both variants collapse to `/rust-wallet/...`, which is benign because the macOS root volume has been read-only (SSV) since 10.15 and a new top-level dir needs /etc/synthetic.conf + reboot. But the depth is install-location-dependent: for a bundle placed four levels under the user's home — e.g. `~/Apps/Hodos/HodosBrowser.app/Contents/MacOS`, or any Downloads/subfolder layout of the same depth — the five-`..` variant resolves to `$HOME/rust-wallet/target/release/hodos-wallet`, a path the user (and anything running as the user, including a browser download or an unpacked archive) can create. The browser would then exec that binary as the wallet: it becomes the money process, binds 31301, and every subsequent wallet_call is served by attacker code. Preconditions are real but narrow — the bundled `Contents/MacOS/hodos-wallet` must be missing or non-executable (a partial DMG copy, a quarantine/extended-attribute failure, an interrupted Sparkle update, or a codesign-strip that clears +x). Note the CI minos guard cannot catch a missing wallet binary: `.github/workflows/release.yml` uses `[ -f "$t" ] || continue`, so an absent hodos-wallet passes that gate green.

findings.title: /wallet/backup/onchain is an ungated FUND-MOVER: it selects UTXOs, signs and broadcasts directly, takes no HttpRequest so dispatch_payment cannot reach it, and is absent from hodos::IsPaymentEndpoint
findings.mechanism: This is a NEW facet of the known-open "73 of 107 Rust routes take no HttpRequest" — the base fact is that they cannot gate themselves; the new fact is that at least one of them BROADCASTS A TRANSACTION rather than merely disclosing data. `handlers.rs :: wallet_backup_onchain` has signature `(state: web::Data<AppState>, _body: web::Bytes)` — no `HttpRequest`, so it can never be routed through `permission_service::dispatch_payment` the way `create_action`, `process_action`, `send_transaction`, `peerpay_send` and `paymail_send` now are. It calls `handlers.rs :: do_onchain_backup`, which does NOT go through `create_action_internal`: it calls `select_utxos_with_preference`, `mark_multiple_spent`, signs with `calculate_sighash(SIGHASH_ALL_FORKID)` and calls `broadcast_transaction` itself. On the C++ side, `PaymentCost.h :: IsPaymentEndpoint` lists createAction / acquireCertificate / sendMessage / transaction/send / peerpay/send / paymail/send / processAction — `/wallet/backup/onchain` is not there, so the interceptor never stamps X-Payment-* headers and never treats it as a spend, which per that header's own ⛔ banner means request_gate substitutes {satoshis:0, cents:0} — under every cap. Reachability: `HttpRequestInterceptor.cpp :: HandleIpcWalletCall` applies NO endpoint allowlist — it forwards whatever endpoint string the page supplied and lets Rust's `domain_trust_mw` decide — and `/wallet/backup/onchain` is not in `is_permission_surface`. So an already-APPROVED dApp origin can POST it. Money moved is miner fee plus the recycled pushdrop/marker sats rather than an arbitrary amount, and `do_onchain_backup` hash-skips when nothing changed, which bounds repetition — hence medium, not high. But it is a spend the user never authorised and the gold pill never announces, and it is the counterexample to any statement that the ungated-route set is disclosure-only.

Everything below I grepped and read myself rather than trusting a comment or a prior claim. All of it is CODE_READING — I am on Windows and cannot execute the macOS tree.

**Mnemonic at rest — SOUND on the shipping path.** `wallet_repo.rs :: create_wallet` does have a plaintext branch (`(mnemonic_phrase.clone(), None)` when `pin` is None, into `wallets.mnemonic TEXT NOT NULL`), but the only frontend caller, `WalletPanelPage.tsx :: doCreateWallet`, always sends `{pin}` after a confirm-PIN flow, and `handlers.rs :: wallet_create` rejects a malformed PIN. So the DB copy is PBKDF2+AES-GCM (`crypto/pin.rs`). The macOS auto-unlock copy is a Keychain generic password, not a file: `crypto/dpapi.rs :: dpapi_encrypt` stores it via security-framework 2.11.1 `set_generic_password` and writes only the 8-byte sentinel `b"KEYCHAIN"` into the DB column. Dev/prod are correctly split by `keychain_service()` (HodosBrowserDev vs HodosBrowser). I did NOT verify the Keychain item's ACL or `kSecAttrAccessible` — that needs `security dump-keychain -a` on a Mac, so I am not claiming anything about it either way.

**No plaintext mnemonic file anywhere.** `json_storage.rs` defines `Wallet { mnemonic: String }` and `JsonStorage::save` → `fs::write`, which would put the phrase in a plaintext JSON file — but it has no live caller. The only `JsonStorage::new` in the tree is `database/migration.rs`'s legacy JSON→SQLite read path; every other `json_storage::` reference is to the unrelated `AddressInfo` struct. Also grepped every `log::`/`println!` site touching "mnemonic" — all of them log `pin.is_some()` / a count / an error string, never the phrase. And `do_onchain_backup` publishes an ENCRYPTED PushDrop, not the phrase, so the on-chain backup is not a disclosure path.

**The macOS dev safeguard is as strong as the Windows one.** `AppPaths::EnforceDevSafeguard` IS called in `cef_browser_shell_mac.mm :: main`, before any `GetAppDirName()` read. Its dev-build predicate does match the macOS bundle layout — the fifth clause `build/bin/HodosBrowser` matches `.../cef-native/build/bin/HodosBrowser.app/Contents/MacOS/HodosBrowser`, and an Xcode multi-config build matches `build/bin/Release`. The Rule-2 scrub uses `unsetenv("HODOS_DEV")` on the non-Windows arm, which mutates `environ`, so the `posix_spawn(..., environ)` children (hodos-wallet, hodos-adblock) inherit the corrected namespace. The Rust wallet carries its own independent `main.rs :: enforce_dev_safeguard`, and `app_dir_name()`/`wallet_port()`/`keychain_service()` all re-read the env each call so a scrub takes effect everywhere. Ports and Keychain services are dev/prod-split. The ONE crack is the child-process env read in process_helper_mac.mm, reported as finding 2.

**ProfileLock's `__APPLE__` arm is sound as same-machine mutual exclusion.** `flock(LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB)` on an `O_CLOEXEC` fd (so no child can inherit and hold it), 6 × 500 ms retry, released in `ReleaseProfileLock`; `cef_browser_shell_mac.mm` fails CLOSED — NSAlert + `return 1` — and picker mode correctly skips the lock and touches no real profile. `ProfileManager.cpp :: RegistryLock`'s macOS arm creates `.profiles.lock` with mode 0600. The lock's real limitation is scope, not correctness: it covers the per-profile dir only, so it says nothing about `<data_root>/wallet/wallet.db` (global, guarded instead by the 31301 bind) and nothing about the helper handles in finding 2. Two different profiles running at once is intended (`LaunchWithProfile` exists for it), and the second instance's `QuickHealthCheck` adopts the first's wallet, so there is normally one writer.

**Backup path confinement is sound.** `backup.rs :: validate_backup_path` + `lexical_normalize_abs` require an absolute path, reject Windows verbatim/UNC/device prefixes, collapse `..` and return None if it escapes above the root, and confine to `backups_dir_for_db()` = `<data_root>/backups`. `Path::starts_with` is component-wise, so a sibling-prefix dir like `/x/backupsevil` does not slip past `/x/backups`. The symlink caveat is already documented in-file and correctly reasoned.

**Not re-derived (settled or owner-deferred):** the concurrency TOCTOU, the 429 balance self-heal, the disclosure set, the bare fact that 73 routes take no HttpRequest, `is_permission_surface` being a string list, and the macOS `wallet_call` SSRF / SyncHttpClient `__APPLE__` arm. Finding 5 is offered only as the new facet that one of those ungated routes broadcasts a transaction.

**Checked and NOT claimed, because it needs measurement I cannot do:** on-disk modes of `wallet.db` (SQLite creates 0644, nothing chmods it) and of `<data_root>` (`create_dir_all` → 0755). Whether that is world-readable in practice depends on `~/Library` being 0700 on the target macOS, which I cannot verify from here — `stat -f '%Sp %N' ~/Library ~/Library/Application\ Support/HodosBrowser/wallet/wallet.db` settles it in one command. Likewise Time Machine inclusion: nothing in the tree sets `NSURLIsExcludedFromBackupKey` or `CSBackupSetItemExcluded` (grepped, zero hits), so the money DB is captured by default backups — normal for a browser profile, but worth an owner decision given it is a wallet.

findings.mechanism: e722539 is explicitly a two-half change ('do both or neither'). It shipped a negative control for the C++ half only: IsPaymentEndpoint.ProcessActionMatches and ComputePaymentCost.ProcessActionUsesTheCreateActionOutputsShape in cef-native/tests/payment_cost_test.cpp, both verified red when the PaymentCost.h line is reverted. WHAT I CONFIRMED (every citation re-grepped; all exist as described):
- `cef-native/mac/process_helper_mac.mm :: main` does call `HistoryManager::GetInstance().Initialize(cache_path)` unconditionally, before `CefExecuteProcess` — i.e. before the process type is known, so all 5 helper bundles (CMakeLists.txt `CEF_HELPER_APP_SUFFIXES`, all built from the same `HODOS_HELPER_SRCS`) run it.
- `HistoryManager::OpenDatabase` is `sqlite3_open_v2(..., SQLITE_OPEN_READWRITE|SQLITE_OPEN_CREATE)` + `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` + `PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL` + `sqlite3_busy_timeout(5000)`.
- The banner in `simple_render_process_handler.cpp :: SimpleRenderProcessHandler::SimpleRenderProcessHandler` and commit 83fe472's message both assert macOS "never ran this init at all". Narrowly true of that constructor (`#ifdef _WIN32`); MISLEADING as stated, because the mac helper's own `main` does it. 83fe472 touched 6 files and `process_helper_mac.mm` was not one of them. That doc inaccuracy is genuine — but it is a comment defect, not a vulnerability.

WHY THE SECURITY CLAIM FAILS:
1. DECISIVE — macOS RUNS WITH NO SANDBOX. `cef_browser_shell_mac.mm :: main` sets `settings.no_sandbox = true;` unconditionally ("CRITICAL: Disable sandbox on macOS for development"); it is the only assignment to `no_sandbox` in the mac tree and carries no build-config guard. An unsandboxed helper can already `open()`/`sqlite3_open_v2()` `<AppSupport>/…/HodosHistory` itself. Our held handle confers ZERO capability a compromised renderer lacks. Commit 83fe472's own rationale was "a hard blocker for enabling the sandbox" — a PREREQUISITE, not a live mitigation. With no sandbox to be a prerequisite for, this is tech debt, not an exploit. "Holds a handle" is not evidence of an exploit.
2. THE HANDLE IS INERT. I grepped all 9 files in `HODOS_HELPER_SRCS` (process_helper_mac.mm, simple_render_process_handler.cpp, NavigationHandler.cpp, AddressHandler.cpp, WalletService_mac.cpp, Logger.cpp, ChildProcessLogSink.cpp, HistoryManager.cpp, IdentityHandler.cpp) for `HistoryManager::`. The ONLY hit outside HistoryManager.cpp itself is the banner COMMENT at simple_render_process_handler.cpp line 453. Post-83fe472 there is no call site in the helper that reads, writes or deletes. "Can forge or erase history" names no code path; a compromised renderer would use raw syscalls, which returns to point 1.
3. THE DEV/PROD HALF IS REFUTED ON ITS OWN PREMISE. The S2 lesson is that the WINDOWS sandbox strips the child environment. macOS sets `no_sandbox = true`, spawns children with inherited `environ`, and nothing in the mac path scrubs it; `cef-native/mac_build_run.sh:66` is `export HODOS_DEV=1` in the parent shell, so the helper's `AppPaths::GetAppDirName()` → `getenv("HODOS_DEV")` returns "1". The finding names no macOS mechanism that would break inheritance — it transplants a Windows-sandbox fact onto an unsandboxed platform. Even granting it, the artifact would be an empty schema-only file (see point 2), not a data leak.
4. THE `"Default"` FALLBACK IS LARGELY DEFUSED. `SimpleApp::OnBeforeChildProcessLaunch` (simple_app.cpp line 69) is platform-neutral — the only `#ifdef _WIN32` in that region spans lines 41–50 — and `cef_browser_shell_mac.mm :: main` builds `CefRefPtr<SimpleApp> app(new SimpleApp())` and passes it to `CefInitialize`, so CEF appends `--profile=<id>` to every macOS child command line too. The fallback fires only if `ProfileManager::IsValidProfileId` rejects the live id.
5. THE `AcquireProfileLock` SUB-CLAIM IS A NON-SEQUITUR. `ProfileLock.cpp` does have an `#elif defined(__APPLE__) || defined(__linux__)` arm, and single-writer discipline over the history DB was never its job. WAL + a 5 s busy timeout is the concurrency design; merely OPENING a WAL DB read-write neither corrupts it nor bypasses the lock.
6. OUT OF PANEL SCOPE. No money movement, no wallet secret, no key linkage, no permission escalation, no gate bypass. Browsing-history privacy at most — and per point 1 there is no capability delta.

ON THE PROPOSED EXPERIMENT: I expect `lsof -c 'HodosBrowser Helper' | grep HodosHistory` to return rows — the OBSERVABLE is probably as predicted. That is precisely why it must not be run as a confirmation: it measures the handle, not the capability delta, and would "pass" against a system where the capability is freely available anyway. The discriminating experiment: from a helper process, attempt `sqlite3_open_v2` on the same path WITHOUT our init (or simply `cat` the file as the helper's uid). If that succeeds — and with `no_sandbox = true` it will — the severity collapses regardless of what lsof shows.

RESIDUAL WORTH KEEPING (LOW, not high, and not this panel's remit): the banner comment and commit message 83fe472 state a macOS property the tree contradicts, and the mac helper carries a gratuitous read-write sqlite handle that becomes a real blocker the day someone flips `no_sandbox` on macOS. Fix = delete the `HistoryManager::Initialize` block in `process_helper_mac.mm` and correct the two doc claims. Negative control for that cleanup: `window.hodosBrowser.history.*` must keep working after removal, since it is IPC-serviced by the browser process.

(d) g_file_dialog_active is set true only in simple_handler.cpp :: SimpleHandler::OnFileDialog (cross-platform, no platform guard) and cleared only in cef_browser_shell.cpp's WM_ACTIVATEAPP; macOS has the definition plus exactly four reads and zero assignments, so the latch is real.

WHY IT IS STILL REFUTED:

1. The creation-time default does not protect the mnemonic on Windows either, so macOS is not weaker where it matters. frontend/src/pages/WalletPanelPage.tsx derives `const preventClose = mnemonic !== null || (pinStep !== null && pendingAction !== null);` and its useEffect([preventClose]) fires on mount with preventClose === false, sending wallet_allow_close. Windows therefore clears its creation-time `true` within milliseconds of React hydrating — long before any mnemonic or PIN screen. When the phrase actually paints, Windows and macOS are in the IDENTICAL state (flag false), and both then depend on the same cross-platform wallet_prevent_close handler in simple_handler.cpp (not inside any #ifdef), which macOS honours at OverlayHelpers_mac.mm:118 and :154. The finding's central sentence — that the unguarded interval is "precisely the window in which the BIP39 recovery phrase is displayed" — is false. The real macOS gap is the interval from NSWindow creation to React's first effect, during which the panel is a loading screen with no secret on it.

2. The proposed experiment would go GREEN and its negative control is uninformative — the same class of defect this project has paid for repeatedly, inverted. Experiment (a) says to click away "at the instant the mnemonic screen paints"; by then prevent_close is true on both platforms, so the overlay survives on macOS today. Adding the flag to the end of the mac creator changes nothing about that observable, so the stated negative control cannot distinguish patched from unpatched.

3. No trust boundary is crossed. No web content participates, nothing is disclosed to a page, no permission gate is bypassed, and no funds move. The worst case is premature dismissal of the user's own overlay, and per CLAUDE.md Invariant #1 the phrase remains reachable through PIN re-verification in the wallet overlay, so "unrecorded" is not permanent.

4. The g_file_dialog_active latch fails in the STICKY direction, not the exposing one. All four macOS readers (InstallProfilePanelClickOutsideMonitor, InstallBookmarksPanelClickOutsideMonitor, InstallSiteInfoPanelClickOutsideMonitor, InstallTabListPanelClickOutsideMonitor in cef_browser_shell_mac.mm) `return event` when the flag is set — the dropdown stops dismissing. Those four panels carry no keys, no balances, no linkage. Further, the wallet cannot be harmed the way claimed: the Windows reason the wallet arm consults g_file_dialog_active is WM_ACTIVATEAPP (cef_browser_shell.cpp:1971), which has no macOS analogue — OverlayHelpers_mac.mm :: InstallAppFocusLossHandler exempts the wallet unconditionally, and cef_browser_shell_mac.mm :: MainWindowDelegate windowDidResignKey (2386-2390) only logs, matching CLAUDE.md.

RESIDUAL, NOT A FINDING: whether NSEvent local monitors fire during a modal NSOpenPanel session is the only route by which the missing macOS file-dialog guard could dismiss the wallet mid-recovery-import. That is unmeasurable from this Windows box and is a macOS UX/robustness ticket (overlay dismisses, user retries the import), not a money-path or disclosure defect. Settling experiment, for the record: on a Mac, open the wallet overlay, use WalletPanelPage's visible recovery file input to open the native picker, then click inside the picker window; RED = the wallet overlay tears down while the picker is up. Control: repeat with the wallet on the mnemonic step (prevent_close true) and confirm it survives, proving the monitor, not the dialog, is the actor.

The underlying divergence (macOS lacks the synchronous creation-time default; g_file_dialog_active never clears on macOS) is a genuine cross-platform inconsistency worth a low-severity UX ticket. It is not a Phase 0.5 trust-boundary finding and not high severity.

REFUTED as filed (high / money-mover); the code reading behind it is CONFIRMED but is a low-severity hygiene defect. I verified every citation myself (CODE_READING only — nothing executed, no wallet running): (a) rust-wallet/src/handlers.rs :: debug_broadcast_nosend does carry the comment "Verify the transaction exists and is in nosend status", and `tx_status` occurs exactly twice in the handler — the tuple binding and one log::info! — with zero comparisons; (b) the sibling handlers.rs :: broadcast_nosend really does guard with `Ok((Some(rt), status)) if status == "nosend"`, and both read the same column (database/transaction_repo.rs :: get_broadcast_status = SELECT status FROM transactions); (c) main.rs registers "/wallet/debug/broadcast-nosend" with no cfg/dev gate; (d) the handler takes (state, web::Json<Value>) so it cannot gate itself, is not under /domain/ or /wallet/session so is_permission_surface misses it, and is absent from hodos::IsPaymentEndpoint (PaymentCost.h lists only createAction, acquireCertificate, sendMessage, /transaction/send, /wallet/peerpay/send, /wallet/paymail/send, /processAction); (e) "wallet_call" IS in IpcMessageAllowedFromWebPage and HandleIpcWalletCall forwards the page-supplied endpoint with no allowlist. So the comment-vs-code mismatch is real. The EXPLOIT is not, for three independent reasons.

1) THE DAMAGING BRANCH IS UNREACHABLE IN THE ASSERTED SCENARIO. Every DB mutation — set_transaction_status(Unproven), mark_spent per input, insert_output for change — sits inside the Ok(msg) arm of broadcast_transaction; the Err arm returns success:false and writes NOTHING. "Resurrect a tx the monitor already failed and whose inputs the wallet has since re-spent" is self-defeating: if a conflicting spend is on-chain, ARC rejects the double-spend and no DB write occurs; if ARC accepts, the spend is genuinely on the network, so re-marking inputs spent and status unproven is convergence toward truth, not corruption.

2) ZERO CAPABILITY GAIN. The body is {txid} only — the caller cannot choose a destination. The tx must already exist fully signed in the wallet DB with outputs the user approved at createAction/pay_402 time, so funds can only go where the user already authorized. And a nosend txid is knowable only to a party that received the BEEF (that IS the nosend delivery mechanism: BRC-121 pay_402 / peerpay), who can submit those exact bytes to ARC directly without the wallet. The endpoint hands an attacker nothing they do not already hold.

3) TWO GATES THE FINDING ELIDES: it is not reachable from "any page" — domain_trust_mw waves through only an ALREADY-APPROVED origin (unknown ones get the 202 connect/domain_approval prompt first) — and validate_beef_ancestry must succeed or the handler 400s before any broadcast.

Net: worth fixing the comment or adding `if tx_status != "nosend" { 400 }` as defense-in-depth, but ARC — not this handler — is the actual authority on whether a written-off tx may re-enter, and no user loses money or privacy via this path.

ONE RESIDUAL WORTH FILING SEPARATELY (independent of the missing status check, same handler, same call): the Ok arm treats outputs[len-1] as our change unconditionally and inserts it with derivation=None, is_change=true whenever no row exists. Output order is request outputs -> service fee -> change, so a spend with NO change makes the last output the 1000-sat Hodos treasury output; inserting that as wallet-owned yields a phantom UTXO — balance inflation plus a derivation-less input candidate for a future spend. Data-integrity bug, not a fund-mover. Experiment that would settle it: dev wallet, pick a confirmed tx with no change output, call the endpoint, then `SELECT * FROM outputs WHERE txid=?` and check for a new is_change=1 row with NULL derivation, and whether coin selection will pick it.

Consequently the "stale comment + release.yml already signs, so the precondition no longer holds" framing is a misdiagnosis: the signing claim is true (verified — helpers, main exe, bundle, wallet, adblock, --options runtime), but signing is not the missing piece; the helper sandbox-entry code and its link dependency are.
